## Natural-language hypothesis

In the hundred-year time-slice PCA on the forms of capital (all 12 Z‑indicators over the 39 slices of capital.csv; PC1 explains ≈30 % of variance; PC1 is sign-fixed so that positive PC1 points along the dominant amber/depot direction), **both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) are characterized by strongly positive PC1 scores — a profile driven above all by social capital expressed through amber (loading +0.75) and, secondarily, by economic capital expressed through depots/hoards (+0.44), against negative contributions from symbolic capital (hatchet/sword, −0.30) and from monument count (−0.29).**

- **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE):** PC1 is positive throughout and **rises across the phase**, from ≈+0.6 at 3400 BCE (the phase minimum) to ≈+1.8 at 3000 BCE (the phase maximum), with a plateau ≈+1.8–1.5 in 3200–3100 BCE. Phase mean ≈ **+1.39** (sd ≈ 0.50).
- **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE):** PC1 is also positive but slightly lower — peaking at ≈+1.6 at 2800 BCE, dipping to ≈+0.7 at 2700 BCE, and **decaying to ≈+0.4 by 2300 BCE** (phase minimum). Phase mean ≈ **+1.13** (sd ≈ 0.44).

So in PC1 terms, the Middle Neolithic is the higher and **rising** high-pole expression of the amber‑/depot-dominated axis, the Younger Neolithic a **still-positive but gradually decaying** expression of the same axis, and both phases sit on the same amber-dominant pole, well above every later phase (Late Neolithic −0.34, Middle Bronze Age −3.13, Younger Bronze Age −1.87, and even slightly below the Early Neolithic baseline +1.77). In terms of the four capital forms, PC1 across these Neolithic phases is dominated by **social capital (amber)** and **economic capital (depots/hoards)**, with a smaller positive **cultural** component (pottery decoration +0.18), opposing **symbolic capital (hatchet/sword)** and monument-based social display.

**PC1 loadings** (positive = amber/depot direction): Zamber (Social) **+0.749**, ZHort (Economic, depot) **+0.435**, Zkeverz (Cultural, decoration) +0.176; ZAxtSchwert (Symbolic, hatchet/sword) **−0.299**, ZMonument (Social, monument count) **−0.292**, and small contributions from ZBeil −0.104, ZCU_AU −0.103, ZMW −0.086, ZKeform −0.075, Zhausgr +0.063, ZSichel +0.059, ZDolch −0.054. Mean loading by form: Social +0.118 (driven by amber), Economic +0.076 (depot), Cultural +0.050, Symbolic −0.097.

**Robustness (sanity check, not headline):** PCA on the four pre-aggregated capital-form indices (locked grouping) yields PC1 with ≈50 % variance and loadings Social −0.64, Cultural +0.63, Symbolic −0.39, Economic +0.21; in that coarser convention the Middle Neolithic sits negative (−0.98) and the Younger Neolithic near zero (+0.25), consistent with the Neolithic occupying a distinct (amber/social-capital) pole apart from the Bronze Age — the sign/scale differs only because aggregating re-weights the variables, so the all-12 PCA above is the headline.

**Pollen (context only, never in the PCA):** slice PC1 correlates r ≈ **−0.73** with pollen openness (SMOOTH_MEAN_100y); both Neolithic phases fall on the less-open, closed-landscape side (mean openness ≈ −0.5), i.e. the amber/depot-high PC1 pole coincides with comparatively closed vegetation, reversing only when PC1 swings negative in the Bronze Age.

payload.workflow: Loaded data/capital.csv (39 hundred-year BCE slices), parsed European decimal commas, standardized the 12 Z-indicators, ran PCA via numpy SVD, sign-fixed PC1 positive = amber/depot direction (amber loading > 0), extracted per-slice PC1, computed MN (3400-3000) and YN/SG (2900-2300) phase statistics and trajectories, reported loadings grouped by the locked four-capital mapping (Symbolic=hatchet/sword+dagger+house size, Social=copper/gold+amber+monument count, Cultural=pottery form+decoration, Economic=depot+sickle+axe/celt+monument size), ran a 4-form-aggregation PCA as a sanity check, and computed a pollen-openness correlation as optional context only.
payload.hypothesis: In the hundred-year time-slice PCA on the forms of capital (PC1 ~30% variance; positive PC1 = amber/depot direction), the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) are both characterized by strongly positive PC1, i.e. a profile dominated by social capital (amber, +0.75) and economic capital (depots/hoards, +0.44) against symbolic capital (hatchet/sword, -0.30) and monument count (-0.29). MN PC1 is positive and rising across the phase (mean +1.39, from +0.6 at 3400 to +1.8 at 3000 BCE); YN PC1 is also positive but slightly lower and decaying (mean +1.13, peaking +1.6 at 2800 BCE, dipping at 2700 BCE, falling to +0.4 by 2300 BCE). Both phases sit on the same high-positive pole well above the Late Neolithic (-0.34) and Bronze Age phases (OBA -3.13, YBA -1.87).
